title: REACTIVE ARTHRITIS: The Triple Threat
summary: A systemic inflammatory condition emerging as a sterile joint response to a distant infection, primarily in the gastrointestinal or urogenital tracts. It is classically recognized by a triad of symptoms affecting the eyes, joints, and urinary system.

sections.title: Clinical Definition
sections.content: Reactive Arthritis (formerly known as Reiter’s Syndrome) is a multi-systemic inflammatory disorder that follows an infection. It belongs to the family of seronegative spondyloarthropathies, meaning Rheumatoid Factor (RF) is typically negative. The condition is characterized by an asymmetric inflammatory arthritis that develops days to weeks after a primary extra-articular infection.

content.mnemonic: Can't See, Can't Pee, Can't Climb a Tree
content.explanation: This represents the classic triad: Conjunctivitis (Can't See), Urethritis/Cervicitis (Can't Pee), and Arthritis (Can't Climb a Tree).

rows: Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Campylobacter jejuni, Clostridium difficile

sections.title: Ophthalmic Manifestations
content: Bilateral Conjunctivitis: The most common ocular finding, often mucopurulent.
Acute Anterior Uveitis: Typically unilateral, recurrent, and characterized by pain, redness, and photophobia.
Episcleritis and Scleritis: Less common but documented.
Keratitis: Punctate epithelial erosions or subepithelial opacities.
Cystoid Macular Edema: Possible complication of severe chronic uveitis.

rows: Psoriatic skin plaques, nail pitting, DIP joint involvement.
Positive cultures for N. gonorrhoeae, migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis.
Symmetric small joint involvement, RF/Anti-CCP positive.
Association with Crohn's or Ulcerative Colitis symptoms.

sections.title: Pathogenesis Process
content: 1. Initial Infection: Mucosal infection (GI or GU) occurs.
2. Immune Activation: Pathogen-derived antigens interact with HLA-B27.
3. Cross-Reactivity: Molecular mimicry leads to T-cell activation against host tissues.
4. Localized Inflammation: Sterile inflammation manifests in joints, eyes, and skin.

sections.title: Red Flags & Complications
content: Severe Vision Loss from uncontrolled Acute Anterior Uveitis.
Permanent Joint Deformity or chronic disability.
